chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from some of his companions, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them):

Regarding the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'And know that whatever you gain of war booty, a fifth belongs to Allah, and to the Messenger, and to the near relatives, and to the orphans, and to the poor, and to the wayfarer.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'The fifth of Allah and the fifth of the Messenger belong to the Imam. The fifth of the near relatives belongs to the relatives of the Messenger and the Imam. The orphans are the orphans of the family of the Messenger, and the poor are among them, and the wayfarers are among them. So they are not taken out from them to others.'

key_terms.يَتَامَى آلِ الرَّسُولِ: Orphans of the family of the Messenger

ai.seo_question: Who is entitled to the Khums according to Shia interpretation of Surah Al-Anfal?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the distribution of Khums by distinguishing the divine share as the Imam's portion, while assigning the Prophet's share and the 'near relatives' (Dhawi al-Qurba) specifically to the Ahl al-Bayt. It further restricts the categories of orphans, poor, and wayfarers to those within the Prophet's lineage, a view supported by Shia scholars who argue this exclusivity prevents the transfer of religious authority to the general community.
